keyTerms.definition: log p(x) = ELBO + KL: ELBO is the tractable expectation, KL the unobservable gap.
p(z|x) = p(x,z)/p(x) pulls log p(x) out of the expectation.

recall.question: Prove the ELBO identity.
recall.answer: KL(q||p(z|x)) = E_q[log q - log p(z|x)]; substitute p(z|x) = p(x,z)/p(x); the log p(x) term pulls out; rearranged: log p(x) = ELBO + KL.

Compare the gradient against the closed form 2 x mu = 2.0.

recall.question: Why does the reparameterized gradient return 0.0?
recall.answer: .detach() on the whole z expression severs the graph. Fix: z = mu + sig * eps with no detach.

recall.answer: Prior (0.54, 0.36, 0.10), marginal 0.590, posterior (0.732, 0.183, 0.085). Old q padded with 0 gives log q_C = -inf: ELBO -inf. The family must grow a third state.

Identical marginal and likelihood, completely different parameters.

recall.question: Give two counterexamples to 'higher ELBO means a better model'.
recall.answer: One: improving q from prior to (0.7,0.3) raises ELBO from -0.6155 to -0.5390 with the model fixed. Two: the label-swapped model has identical marginal and likelihood with completely different parameters.
